subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: being open with clients about AI use [Action]
passage: Before the contract began, Sarita and Keerthana sat with the school trust's secretary in the Palampur office. Sarita said plainly, 'For the first draft of the newsletter we sometimes use an AI tool, and one of us always checks and edits every line.' Keerthana added that names, fee lists and children's details would never be typed into any such tool. The secretary was quiet, then asked what the tool would be used for, and Sarita showed a sample draft with the edits marked. 'Thank you for telling us,' the secretary said. 'Last year a vendor told us nothing and we found out from a parent.' The secretary asked for the promise to be written into the contract, and Keerthana added a line that same evening.

qa.q: What would never be typed into any such tool?
qa.a: Names, fee lists and children's details would never be typed into any such tool.

qa.q: What did Sarita want the secretary to see by showing the sample draft?
qa.a: Sarita wanted to reassure the secretary that a person checks and edits every line, so the secretary could feel confident the AI use was under control.

qa.q: What could the team do to keep the trust after signing?
qa.a: They could send a short note each quarter saying how AI was used, since repeated honesty keeps the promise alive.

qa.q: What would change for the secretary if the team had said nothing and the truth came out later?
qa.a: The secretary would likely feel misled, as with the vendor last year, and trust would drop, so no promise would have been written into the contract.

grounding: Shows a team telling a client where AI assists in delivery and confirming what data is never shared with tools.
